items.title: Section: What "One Mind" Really Means — A Single Reverent Thought, and Countless Moments Mistaken for One

items.zh: 如是已思擇色蘊。我次當說名所攝四無色蘊隨所應建立相。如本地分立一心相，今先顯示。如世尊言：若有眾生於如來所，但發一心及一言說：善逝大師！善逝大師！如是發心，我尚說彼於諸善法多有所作，何況身語如其心量隨順奉行。又如是言：由一淨心，當往善趣。如是等類，當知此中依轉所攝相續一心，由世俗道名發一心。又依世俗相續道理，名發一語及發身業。
items.en: Having now analysed form aggregate, I shall next explain the character to be established for the four formless aggregates subsumed under name. As the character of one mind was established in the Basic Section, this is now clarified. As the World-Honoured One said: if any being, in the presence of the Tathāgata, merely generates one thought and speaks one utterance — "Well-Gone One! Great Teacher!" — I say that being has already accomplished much among wholesome phenomena, how much more so one who acts with body and speech according to that same intention. And it is also said: through one pure thought, one is destined for a fortunate rebirth. Things of this kind should be understood, in this context, as one mind in the sense of a continuous succession, subsumed under its ongoing operation, called "generating one mind" according to conventional expression. And according to this same conventional principle of continuity, one likewise speaks of generating one utterance or one bodily action.

items.title: Section: Why the Discriminating and Non-Discriminating Minds Always Share the Same Object

items.zh: 問：有分別心、無分別心，當言同緣現在境耶？為不同耶？答：當言同緣現在境界。何以故？由三因故。謂極明了故，於彼作意故，二依資養故。
items.en: Question: should the discriminating mind and the non-discriminating mind be said to take the same present object, or not? Answer: they should be said to take the same present object. Why? For three reasons: because of utter clarity, because of shared attention towards that object, and because both are nourished by the same dependence.

items.title: Section: Mind Is Never Itself Defiled — Only Ever Accompanied by What Defiles It

items.zh: 問：染心生時，當言自性故染？為相應故，為隨眠故？答：當言相應故、隨眠故，非自性故。若彼自性是染污者，應如貪等畢竟不淨。若爾，大過。由彼自性不染污故，說心生時自性清淨。
items.en: Question: when a defiled mind arises, should this be said to belong to its own essential nature, to association, or to latent seeds? Answer: it should be said to belong to association and to latent seeds, not to its own essential nature. If its own essential nature were defiled, it would have to be irredeemably impure like craving and the rest. If this were so, a great fault would follow. Because its own essential nature is not defiled, it is said that mind, when it arises, is essentially pure.

items.title: Section: Affliction Clings Through Association, and Its Dormant Seed Weighs the Whole Being Down

items.zh: 問：諸煩惱纏，於心二種染污因中，當言何等？答：當言相應。問：此中何等說名隨眠？答：諸煩惱品所有麁重不安隱性。又持諸行令成苦性。是故聖者，由行苦故現觀為苦，於諸行中安住苦觀。云何觀耶？如毒熱癰，乃至廣說如有尋有伺地，應如是觀。
items.en: Question: among the two causes of mental defilement, what role do manifest afflictions play? Answer: they belong to association. Question: what here is called the latent seed? Answer: the heaviness and lack of ease belonging to the whole category of affliction. It further sustains conditioned phenomena in an unsatisfactory state. Therefore the noble ones, directly perceiving suffering through the suffering of formations, dwell in settled contemplation of suffering amid all conditioned phenomena. How is this contemplated? Like a feverish, painful abscess, as extensively explained in the Stage With Both Investigation and Analysis — one should contemplate accordingly.

items.title: Section: Three Kinds of Defilement, and the Five Ropes That Bound the Defeated Asura King

items.zh: 復有三種染惱心法，當知普攝一切染惱。所謂業染惱、受染惱、煩惱染惱。初二染惱，唯欲界繫；最後染惱，通三界繫。問：何等名為心煩惱縛？答：一切隨眠。
items.en: There are also three kinds of defiling mental factor, encompassing all defilement altogether: defilement through karma, defilement through feeling, and defilement through affliction. The first two belong only to the desire realm; the last extends throughout all three realms. Question: what is called the mind's bondage through affliction? Answer: every latent seed.

items.zh: 問：何等名業縛？答：樂著事業，名為業縛。

items.title: Section: The Novice Who Longed to Be a Dragon — Karma's Remaining Bonds and Their Six-or-Four-Fold Count

items.zh: 又於三處為障礙業，亦名業縛。謂於出離心，於得出離喜樂，於得聖道。又順異熟障業，亦名業縛。又邪願業，亦名業縛。如是四種，別開有六，總合為四。
items.en: Karma that obstructs three places is also called bondage: obstructing the intention to renounce, obstructing the joy of attaining seclusion, and obstructing attainment of the noble path. Karma bringing about a difficult ripened condition is also called bondage. Karma arising from a misguided aspiration is also called bondage. These four, distinguished separately, become six; combined together, they total four.

items.title: Section: Five Mental Factors in Every Single Moment of Mind — Attention, Contact, Feeling, Perception, and Volition

items.zh: 問：諸識生時，與幾遍行心法俱起？答：五。一、作意，二、觸，三、受，四、想，五、思。問：復與幾不遍行心法俱起？答：不遍行法乃有多種，勝者唯五。一、欲，二、勝解，三、念，四、三摩地，五、慧。作意云何？謂能引發心法。觸云何？謂三和合故，能攝受義。受云何？謂三和合故，能領納義。想云何？謂三和合故，施設所緣，假合而取。此復二種。一、隨覺想，二、言說隨眠想。隨覺想者，謂善言說人天等想。言說隨眠想者，謂不善言說嬰兒等類，乃至禽獸等想。思云何？謂三和合故，令心造作，於所緣境隨與領納、和合、乖離。
items.en:
Question: how many universal mental factors arise together whenever any consciousness arises? Answer: five — attention, contact, feeling, perception, and volition. Question: with how many non-universal mental factors does it further arise? Answer: non-universal factors are of many kinds, but the strongest are five — aspiration, resolve, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom.
What is attention? That which rouses mind towards its object. What is contact? The meeting of the three, capable of grasping the object. What is feeling? The meeting of the three, capable of receiving the object. What is perception? The meeting of the three, establishing a label for the object and grasping it through that borrowed label — this is further of two kinds: articulate perception, and dormant, language-latent perception. What is volition? The meeting of the three, causing mind to act, either going along with and receiving, uniting with, or separating from the object.

items.title: Section: Five Further Factors — Aspiration, Resolve, Mindfulness, Concentration, and Wisdom's Threefold Discernment

items.zh: 欲云何？謂於彼彼境界，隨趣希樂。勝解云何？謂於彼彼境界，隨趣印可。念云何？謂於彼彼境界，隨趣明記。三摩地云何？謂於彼彼境界，隨順趣向為審慮依心一境性。慧云何？謂於彼彼境界，隨順趣向簡擇諸法。或如理觀察，或不如理觀察，或非如理非不如理觀察。
items.en: What is aspiration? Inclining towards and wishing for a particular object. What is resolve? Inclining towards and affirming a particular object. What is mindfulness? Inclining towards and clearly retaining a particular object. What is concentration? Inclining towards a particular object as the basis for careful reflection and one-pointedness of mind. What is wisdom? Inclining towards a particular object with discernment of phenomena — whether reasonable, unreasonable, or neither.

items.title: Section: What Each Mental Factor Actually Does — From Rousing the Mind to Judging Right and Wrong

items.zh: 復次，作意為何業？謂於所緣引心為業。觸為何業？謂受、想、思所依為業。受為何業？謂愛生所待為業。想為何業？謂於所緣，令心彩畫言說為業。思為何業？謂發起尋、伺、身語業為業。
items.en: Furthermore, what is attention's function? Drawing mind towards its object. What is contact's function? Serving as the basis for feeling, perception, and volition. What is feeling's function? Serving as the condition craving depends upon. What is perception's function? Painting and narrating mind's own object. What is volition's function? Giving rise to investigation, analysis, and bodily and verbal action.

items.title: Section: Aspiration Fuels the Effort, Concentration Grounds the Wisdom, and Wisdom Judges What Is Pure

items.zh: 欲為何業？謂發生勤勵為業。勝解為何業？謂於所緣功德、過失、或俱相違，印持為業。念為何業？謂於久所思、所作、所說記憶為業。三摩地為何業？謂智所依為業。慧為何業？謂於言論所行染污、清淨，隨順考察為業。
items.en: What is aspiration's function? Generating diligent effort. What is resolve's function? Affirming merit, fault, or neither in an object. What is mindfulness's function? Remembering what was long ago thought, done, or said. What is concentration's function? Serving as the basis for knowledge. What is wisdom's function? Investigating, in accordance with reason, whether speech and conduct are defiled or pure.

blocks.text: Fascicle 55 continues the analysis of mind. Its opening claim is one of the most important in Buddhism: the mind is not defiled by its own nature.
A continuous mind of the active consciousnesses is, by convention, called "one mind". Master Cháng Bǎi: mind continuing in similarity is called one mind, though many moments pass.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the discriminating mental consciousness and the non-discriminating five senses take the same present object.

Defilement comes through association and latent seeds, not through mind's own nature; if mind were defiled by nature, it would be impure forever, like craving. Master Cháng Bǎi: "pure" here does not mean uncontaminated purity; it means that greed, hatred, and delusion are not mind's nature, so beings can be freed.
Master Cháng Bǎi: even without painful or changing feeling, the seeds of affliction follow the aggregates and give them the suffering of conditioning.
Every latent seed is the mind's bondage. Master Cháng Bǎi: affliction binds beings like a rope, so that body and mind lack freedom.
Master Cháng Bǎi: one who makes merit wishing to become a nāga or garuḍa, or an outsider seeking heaven, creates karma of misguided aspiration.
Attention, contact, feeling, perception, and volition accompany every mind. Master Cháng Bǎi: perception takes marks, which needs words; even beings without language have seeds of speech.

Aspiration, resolve, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. Resolve is "inclining towards and affirming an object". Wisdom discerns things reasonably, unreasonably, or neither, so as a mental factor it can be good, bad, or neutral.

Attention draws mind to its object; contact is the basis of feeling; feeling is what craving relies on. Master Cháng Bǎi: without attention one looks without seeing. On concentration: to reach the noble path, concentration is the foundation.
"If mind were defiled by nature, it would be impure forever." The whole possibility of practice rests on this sentence.

quiz.q: The English has "a continuous succession subsumed under one mind." What is wrong, and what is "one mind" here?
options: nothing is wrong: the succession truly falls under one abiding mind, the English is exact, and one mind means the unchanging original mind
the direction is right, but one mind means a single moment, so "succession" is wrong
the direction is reversed: the continuous one mind falls under the active consciousnesses; "one" is a similar continuum spanning many moments
one mind means the store-consciousness, and the English should say so
quiz.why: The Chinese says a continuous one mind subsumed under the active consciousnesses is, by conventional usage, called generating one mind. Master Cháng Bǎi: mind continuing in similarity is called one mind, though many moments have passed. The English "subsumed under one mind" turns this around, as if a succession were contained in a single mind.

quiz.q: For what three reasons do the discriminating and non-discriminating minds take the same present object?
options: one seed, one karma, and one result, so they must take the same present object and could never take different ones
a faculty, an object, and light
investigation, analysis, and perception
utter clarity, attention towards that object, and nourishment of the two supports
quiz.why: The treatise gives three reasons. Master Cháng Bǎi: the discriminating mind of mental consciousness and the non-discriminating mind of the five take the same present object; hence when the five consciousnesses arise, the sixth is surely among them. This is why the arising of a sense-consciousness is never mere sensation alone.

quiz.q: When a defiled mind arises, where does the defilement lie, according to the treatise?
options: in its own nature, for mind is defiled from the start, and only ending mind brings purity, so practice means ending mind
in outer objects, which defile the mind
in association and latent seeds, not in its own nature
in its nature and association, not latent seeds
quiz.why: The treatise answers that defilement comes through association and latent seeds, not its own nature; if mind were defiled by nature, it would be finally impure like craving. Master Cháng Bǎi: mind is defiled because it is joined with defiled factors and followed by seeds of affliction, not because mind itself is defiled.

quiz.q: What does "essentially pure" mean, per Master Cháng Bǎi, and what follows if mind were defiled by nature?
options: it is uncontaminated purity, beings being already buddhas, so no practice is needed; only if mind were defiled would practice mean anything
it means mind holds no seeds; only if defiled could seeds exist
not being defiled by nature is called pure, not uncontaminated purity; were mind defiled by nature, beings could never achieve the path
it means mind joins no factor; only if defiled would factors arise
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the nature of mind itself not being defiled is called pure, and this does not mean uncontaminated purity. If mind inherently had greed, hatred, and delusion, it would be impure forever, and beings would have no chance to achieve the noble path. So the phrase protects the possibility of practice; it does not claim beings are already awakened.

quiz.q: The English has "through this pervasive impermanence" for 由行苦故. What is lost?
options: 現觀 is mistranslated: the Chinese means inference, so "directly perceiving" is wrong
nothing is lost: 行苦 simply means impermanence, and the English is clearer, with no need for the three sufferings
聖者 is mistranslated: the Chinese speaks of ordinary beings
the name 行苦 is lost: painful feeling is suffering itself, pleasant feeling change, neutral feeling formations; the English turns this into impermanence
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: even when the aggregates have neither the suffering of pain nor of change, seeds of affliction follow them and give them the nature of the suffering of formations. Painful feeling is suffering itself, pleasant feeling change, and neutral feeling formations. The English "pervasive impermanence" drops this technical term, on which the whole sentence turns.

quiz.q: Which realms do the three kinds of defilement belong to?
options: karma and feeling belong only to the desire realm; affliction extends throughout the three
affliction belongs only to the desire realm; karma and feeling extend throughout the three
all three exist only in the desire realm, beings of the higher realms having no defilement whatsoever
all three extend throughout the three realms, with no difference
quiz.why: The treatise says the first two belong only to the desire realm, and the last extends throughout the three. Master Cháng Bǎi: only desire-realm beings have defilement through karma and feeling; formless beings are joined only with neutral feeling. Afflictions, though light, persist above, which is why the third extends through all realms.

quiz.q: What is the mind's bondage through affliction, and what image does Master Cháng Bǎi use?
options: all manifest bindings; affliction burns beings like a fire
every latent seed; affliction, like a rope, binds beings fast, leaving body and mind without freedom
all evil karma; karma holds beings like a prison until the sentence ends, whence the name bondage
all painful feeling; feeling strikes beings like a poisoned arrow
quiz.why: The treatise answers that every latent seed is the mind's bondage through affliction. Master Cháng Bǎi: when beings dwell with affliction, it binds them fast like a rope, so that body and mind lack freedom. Note the treatise says latent seeds, not merely manifest afflictions.

quiz.q: Why is karma of misguided aspiration a bond, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: one makes merit vowing to be a nāga, garuḍa, or god; not knowing the three realms are suffering, effort gains only temporary ease
because making any vow is itself wrong, so even a bodhisattva's great vow is misguided karma
because a misguided vow surely brings hell
because such a vow obstructs others' practice
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one who makes merit with a wish to become a nāga or garuḍa, or outsiders seeking heaven, create karma of misguided aspiration. Not knowing that results in the three realms are suffering, and vowing rebirth there, even diligent practice gains only temporary ease. So what binds is the aim, not the merit itself.

quiz.q: Which five universal and five strongest non-universal factors arise with consciousness?
options: universal: aspiration, resolve, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom; non-universal: attention, contact, feeling, perception, volition
universal: craving, aversion, ignorance, pride, doubt; non-universal: faith, shame, conscience, non-greed, non-hatred, divided by good and evil
universal: attention, contact, feeling, perception, volition; non-universal: aspiration, resolve, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom
universal: the five aggregates; non-universal: the five faculties
quiz.why: The treatise names attention, contact, feeling, perception, and volition, and among non-universal factors aspiration, resolve, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: the five pervade all consciousnesses, places, times, and moral qualities; the others are sometimes present and sometimes not, and are also called object-specific factors.

quiz.q: The English has "either drawing towards, uniting with, or separating from the object." What is the problem?
options: 隨與領納 is not "drawing towards"; the three correspond to neutral, pleasant, and painful feeling
all three are forms of craving, and should be so rendered, since volition works only in craving
和合 means sexual union, and should be so rendered
乖離 means a schism in the community, and should be so rendered
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with neutral feeling this is called following along in receiving; with pleasant feeling, following along in union; with painful feeling, following along in separation. So the three name volition's work in the three feelings. "Drawing towards" misreads the first, which is receiving, and sounds too much like the second.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 勝解?
options: the most excellent wisdom, found only in noble ones, its object always the true Dharma and never a wrong view
a mind wishing to obtain the object
a strong, excellent understanding of an object, unshakable once arisen, and just as unshakable when its object is a wrong view
not forgetting what has been experienced
quiz.why: The treatise defines 勝解 as inclining towards and affirming an object. Master Cháng Bǎi: it is a strong cognition of the object; once such an understanding arises it is not shaken, and likewise when its object is a wrong view. So it is morally open. "Resolve" leans towards will, and the sense of cognitive certainty rests on the word "affirming."

quiz.q: In what ways does the treatise say wisdom observes phenomena?
options: only reasonably, for wisdom is always good, and what is unreasonable cannot be called wisdom at all
by hearing, reflection, and cultivation
worldly and supramundane
reasonably, unreasonably, or neither
quiz.why: The treatise says wisdom discerns phenomena reasonably, unreasonably, or neither. As a mental factor it is thus open to all three moral qualities. Master Cháng Bǎi, speaking of the perfection, says that of the six perfections the first five can be shared with ordinary beings and outsiders, and only prajñā is distinctive. So "wisdom" here is broader than prajñā.

quiz.q: What is attention's function, and what happens without it?
options: serving as the basis of feeling, perception, and volition, which have no support without it
giving rise to investigation and bodily and verbal action; without it one cannot move or speak, which is its chief function
drawing mind towards its object; without it, one looks without seeing and listens without hearing
serving as the basis of wisdom, which cannot exist without it
quiz.why: The treatise says attention's function is drawing mind towards its object. Master Cháng Bǎi: even with an unimpaired faculty and a present object, without attention leading the mind towards the object one looks without seeing and listens without hearing. The other options are the functions of contact, volition, and concentration.

quiz.q: What is feeling's function, and how do contact and feeling stand in order?
options: it causes mind to paint and narrate; feeling arises before contact
it is what the arising of craving relies on; contact must already exist before feeling, perception, and volition function
it affirms merit and fault; feeling and contact have no order or dependence, arising independently of each other
it generates effort; feeling comes after volition
quiz.why: The treatise says contact serves as the basis of feeling, perception, and volition, and feeling is what craving relies on to arise. Master Cháng Bǎi: contact must be present before these functions; and all beings wish to leave pain and gain pleasure, which is craving, and this craving comes from feeling. This is the link 受緣愛.

quiz.q: What are the functions of aspiration and resolve?
options: aspiration remembers what was long ago thought, done, or said; resolve is the basis of wisdom
aspiration draws mind to its object; resolve investigates defilement and purity in speech, both arising first among particular factors
aspiration is what craving relies on; resolve paints and narrates
aspiration generates diligent effort; resolve affirms merit, fault, or neither in an object
quiz.why: The treatise says aspiration generates diligent effort, and resolve affirms merit, fault, or neither. Master Cháng Bǎi: aspiration is having a wish, urging oneself on and rousing the power of diligence; while doubt about the object, unable to settle right and wrong, leaves no resolve. Thus doubt and resolve exclude each other.

quiz.q: The English has "the basis for wisdom" for 智所依, and "wisdom" again for 慧. What is the problem?
options: 智 is worldly cleverness, and should be "cleverness," concentration having nothing to do with the path or severing affliction
智 and 慧 are both "wisdom," hiding the difference; the lecture says achieving the path and severing affliction needs concentration as a base
concentration results from wisdom, so "basis" reverses it
no problem: 智 and 慧 are wholly synonymous in consciousness-only
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: to achieve the noble path and sever afflictions, concentration is surely needed as a foundation. Thus the 智 based on concentration is the knowing that accomplishes the path, while 慧 in the next sentence is the general factor of discernment, open to all moral qualities. Giving both as "wisdom" hides the distinction.
